newsitem.title: USA: Michigan governor signs gasoline tax increase.
newsitem.headline: Michigan governor signs gasoline tax increase.

text.p: Michigan Gov. John Engler on Friday signed a gasoline tax increase of four cents a gallon to help fund the state's transportation system.
The tax increase effective August 1 will raise nearly $200 million a year for road and bridge repairs as part of a state transportation package approved by lawmakers earlier in July.
The plan also includes a 30 percent increase in truck fees generating $43 million, $43 million from the state's general fund and $28 million from wider application of the diesel fuel tax.

Engler also approved legislation appropriating $69 million of interest from the state's budget stabilization fund and $20 million of supplemental appropriations for road repairs in the current fiscal year.
